name: Rex MD
description: Men's telehealth brand (ED, weight loss, testosterone) that sells one hair-loss product: generic finasteride tablets on a quarterly plan.

products.name: Finasteride ("The Finasteride Regrowth Plan")
products.actives: Finasteride 1 mg tablet, once daily, 90-day supply
products.price: From US$13.50 a month (advertised with a 50% first-order saving); sold only as quarterly plans

consultation: Free online question-and-answer form; a US-licensed provider reviews it and may follow up by chat or email (audio or video call in states that require it). Free 2-day shipping.
distinctive: Nothing new in hair: a single low-price generic. Its strength is price and a large men's-health customer base. Its own pages mention minoxidil but list no minoxidil product.
sizeSignal: Site-wide claims: "Over 475,000" men and "58+ million doses" delivered (all conditions, not hair alone).

name: Lemonaid Health
description: General telehealth service offering generic finasteride and a compounded three-in-one scalp spray for men.
audience: Men only (the page says it cannot treat anyone whose birth sex is female).

products.name: Generic finasteride
products.actives: Finasteride 1 mg tablet
products.price: Price not shown on the page; US$25 online visit; shipped free in 3-month supplies; "$30 off first delivery" offer

products.name: Headstrong Spray Rx
products.actives: Minoxidil 5% + finasteride 0.3% + tretinoin 0.015% scalp spray (propylene glycol and alcohol base), once daily

consultation: Online assessment (about 5 minutes) reviewed by a clinician within 24 hours; immediate video visit in some states. US$25 visit fee for the finasteride route. Messaging with clinicians included.
distinctive: The Headstrong spray adds tretinoin (thought to help minoxidil absorb) to topical finasteride and minoxidil in one once-daily spray.
sizeSignal: No hair-specific numbers published. Mid-size general telehealth brand.

name: Sesame (and Costco member pricing)
description: A cash-price marketplace for video visits with independent clinicians, including dermatologists; prescriptions go to the patient's own pharmacy. Costco members get discounted Sesame visits.
audience: Men and women, with or without insurance.

products.name: Hair-loss video visit
products.actives: Clinician may prescribe finasteride, dutasteride, minoxidil (including prescription strength) or spironolactone; medicines are collected from a local pharmacy
products.price: Set by each provider and shown up front (one review site quotes about US$29 for a first hair-loss visit; unverified)

products.name: Skincare Rx subscription
products.actives: Ongoing dermatology care: video visits, unlimited messaging, same-day prescriptions and refills

products.name: Costco member virtual appointment
products.actives: Visit for a new prescription or refill, after verifying Costco membership
products.price: US$29, plus 10% off other Sesame services

consultation: Real-time video visit with a named clinician chosen by the patient (reviews, times and prices shown). No insurance accepted; card, HSA or FSA.
distinctive: A marketplace, not a product brand: the patient picks a named dermatologist and a price, then uses any pharmacy (often very cheap generics). Offers dutasteride and spironolactone, which many questionnaire-only brands avoid. Retail partnership with Costco.
sizeSignal: Costco partnership announced September 2023 (wide national press coverage). No hair-specific numbers.

name: Nurx
description: Women's telehealth brand (it calls Keeps its partner for men; shared ownership under Thirty Madison is widely reported but was not re-verified in this sweep) with a women's hair-loss service built around a compounded spray and oral minoxidil.
audience: Women with female pattern hair loss or traction alopecia. Men are sent to sister brand Keeps. Does not treat telogen effluvium, alopecia areata or scarring alopecia (CCCA).

products.name: Nurx RegrowRx Spray
products.actives: Minoxidil 5% + melatonin 0.1% + tretinoin 0.01% + caffeine 0.2% (compounded, prescription only)
products.price: Not itemised; "most women's hair loss patients pay about $20 a month"

products.name: Minoxidil foam
products.actives: Minoxidil 5% foam

products.name: Oral minoxidil
products.actives: Minoxidil tablet (strength not stated)

products.name: Scalp treatments
products.actives: Ketoconazole 2% cream (60 g); selenium sulfide shampoo

consultation: Health questions plus photos of hair and scalp, no appointment; a licensed provider reviews in a couple of days. One-off US$80 consultation fee covers a scheduled check-in and a year of unlimited messaging. No insurance; HSA/FSA accepted.
distinctive: Melatonin and caffeine added to a minoxidil and tretinoin spray (a hormone-free combination for women). Clear list of the hair-loss types it will not treat. Year-long care fee instead of a monthly membership.
sizeSignal: No hair-specific numbers published.

name: Wisp
description: Women's sexual and reproductive telehealth brand that now sells oral minoxidil and spironolactone for hormonal hair loss.
audience: Women: female pattern hair loss, perimenopause and menopause, postpartum, PCOS.

products.name: Oral Minoxidil
products.actives: Minoxidil tablet, once daily (strength not shown)

products.name: Oral Spironolactone
products.actives: Spironolactone 50 mg or 100 mg tablets

consultation: Medical intake form, with a phone or video call when needed; an independent physician decides. Prescription can be sent to any pharmacy, usually within 3 hours.
distinctive: Sells hair-loss tablets one-off as well as on subscription, and positions them inside menopause and PCOS care (links to a menopause consult and a symptoms quiz).
sizeSignal: No hair-specific numbers found.

name: Amazon One Medical (Pay-per-visit) and Amazon Pharmacy
description: Amazon's flat-fee telehealth: a message or video visit for men's hair loss, with generic medicine delivered by Amazon Pharmacy.
audience: Men aged 18 to 64 (also transgender women, and transgender men on testosterone). Women with hair loss are told telehealth is not the right route. Not for people on Medicare or Medicaid.

products.name: Pay-per-visit consultation
products.actives: Message visit or video visit; 14 days of follow-up messages
products.price: US$29 message visit (where available); US$49 video visit

products.name: Finasteride via Amazon Pharmacy
products.actives: Finasteride tablets, 90-day supply
products.price: Search result of the live page: "from $39" for visit plus 90-day supply; launch coverage (Nov 2024) quoted US$16 a month. Check live page

products.name: Minoxidil 5%
products.actives: Topical minoxidil 5% (over the counter)

consultation: Check-in with an AI assistant ("Health AI"), then a One Medical provider by message or video; prescription sent to Amazon Pharmacy or any pharmacy. Oral minoxidil is not offered (Amazon says it needs lab tests first). Men with a prostate condition or family history of prostate cancer are sent elsewhere.
distinctive: Lowest all-in price from a household name, with fast free delivery for Prime members. Conservative clinical scope: only licensed finasteride and topical minoxidil, no compounding, no women.
sizeSignal: Amazon. The November 2024 launch of fixed prices for hair loss knocked Hims & Hers shares down about 15% in a day (NBC/CNBC report).

name: GoodRx for Hair Loss
description: The drug-discount company's own men's hair-loss subscription, launched October 2025: one price covers the online visit, generic tablets and delivery.

products.name: Finasteride (generic Propecia)
products.actives: Finasteride 1 mg tablet
products.price: As low as US$16 a month

products.name: Oral minoxidil
products.actives: Minoxidil 2.5 mg tablet (off-label)
products.price: As low as US$20 a month

consultation: Online telehealth visit included in the subscription price; cancel any time. (The GoodRx page blocked automated reading, so details come from the press release and search summaries.)
distinctive: "One clear price" for visit, medicine and delivery from a brand people already use to compare pharmacy prices. No compounded or topical products.
sizeSignal: GoodRx is a listed US company with a very large drug-price-comparison audience; no hair subscriber numbers published.

name: Curology (Hair FormulaRx)
description: The personalised prescription skincare brand's move into hair (February 2024): a custom compounded scalp serum for pattern hair loss.
audience: Men and women with androgenetic alopecia.

products.name: Hair FormulaRx
products.actives: Custom topical: three actives chosen by the provider from minoxidil, finasteride, ketoconazole, spironolactone, caffeine and melatonin (strengths not published; minoxidil said to be above over-the-counter strength)
products.price: First box US$24.99 for new subscribers; ongoing price not shown on the page; subscription required

consultation: Online skin-style consultation with photos; a licensed dermatology provider customises the formula. Asynchronous.
distinctive: The "three actives from a menu of six" model copied from its acne business, in one bottle. Topical spironolactone and melatonin as options. Sold in the same account as a customer's skincare.
sizeSignal: Well-known US personalised prescription-skincare subscription brand; hair launched 1 Feb 2024 (trade press). No hair numbers published.

name: Bosley (BosleyRx and BosleyMD)
description: Large US hair-transplant chain (it calls itself "America's #1 Hair Restoration Experts"). BosleyRx is its telehealth prescription arm; BosleyMD is its shop and salon range of shampoos, minoxidil and supplements.
audience: Men and women (BosleyRx lists men's hair loss, women's hair loss and men's sexual health).

products.name: Finasteride
products.actives: Finasteride 1 mg tablet
products.price: From US$17.50 a month (Bosley's own page); "first month free on select products"

products.name: Finasteride + Minoxidil kit
products.actives: Finasteride 1 mg tablet + minoxidil 5% topical

products.name: Oral minoxidil
products.actives: Minoxidil 2.5 mg tablet (off-label)

products.name: Compounded oral finasteride and minoxidil
products.actives: Finasteride + minoxidil in one compounded oral product (strengths not shown)

products.name: BosleyMD range (non-prescription)
products.actives: Minoxidil 5% (men) and 2% (women), shampoos, serums, supplements
products.price: Third-party estimate only: shampoos US$25-40, serums US$45-85 (unverified)

consultation: "Fast, online telehealth visits" (questionnaire reviewed by a provider). Orders are one-off shipments by default; auto-refill every 3, 6 or 12 months is optional.
distinctive: The only large player that runs the whole ladder: shop products, prescriptions, then surgery. One-off shipment by default (no forced subscription).
sizeSignal: "Over 1 million patients served" and "over 50 years of experience" (company claims, mostly transplants). BosleyRx launched November 2020.

name: Miiskin
description: A dermatology app and platform that connects patients with independent US board-certified dermatologists, who can prescribe a wide menu of compounded hair formulas from partner pharmacies.
audience: Men and women; state coverage depends on the dermatologist.

products.name: Single-ingredient compounded items
products.actives: Minoxidil, finasteride or dutasteride (topical or oral, via partner pharmacy)

products.name: Compounded combinations
products.actives: For example minoxidil + finasteride; minoxidil + dutasteride; combinations including latanoprost
products.price: US$48.99 (minoxidil + finasteride) up to US$68.99 (combinations with latanoprost)

products.name: Dermatologist consultation
products.actives: Photo-based, asynchronous
products.price: US$59 first consult; about US$30-49 follow-up (pages differ)

consultation: Photo-based consultation in an app with a named board-certified dermatologist; reply in 1 to 2 working days. No subscription; the patient can choose their pharmacy.
distinctive: Real dermatologists and the widest public menu of unusual actives at fixed prices: topical dutasteride and latanoprost.
sizeSignal: Small in hair. No customer numbers published.

name: Alloy Women's Health
description: Menopause telehealth brand with a "Hair, Lash & Brow" line: oral minoxidil, spironolactone and a prescription lash and brow serum, prescribed by menopause-trained doctors.

products.name: Low-Dose Oral Minoxidil
products.actives: Minoxidil with vitamin D (ingredients listed as "minoxidil, vitamin D, and cellulose"; a customer review describes compounded minoxidil 1 mg / vitamin D 1000 IU capsules, so this appears to be compounded: inferred); 90-day supply

products.name: Spironolactone
products.actives: Spironolactone tablets (anti-androgen)

products.name: Lash & Brow Serum Rx
products.actives: Generic Latisse (bimatoprost) solution

consultation: Online intake reviewed by a menopause-trained, board-certified doctor; free unlimited doctor messaging. Hair products can sit alongside HRT in one plan.
distinctive: Hair loss treated as a menopause symptom next to HRT. Oral minoxidil combined with vitamin D. Bundle discount for stacking (two products save US$30, three save US$60). Lash and brow regrowth sold with scalp hair.
sizeSignal: No hair-specific numbers found.

name: Midi Health
description: Insurance-covered virtual menopause clinic that treats midlife hair thinning as part of a wider care plan.
audience: Women in perimenopause and menopause; all 50 states (not Medicare).

products.name: Hair Regrowth Serum / Minoxidil/Finasteride Hair Regrowth Spray
products.actives: Compounded topical minoxidil + finasteride (strengths not shown)
products.price: Not shown; visits billed to insurance

products.name: Oral options named in Midi's guides
products.actives: Oral minoxidil; spironolactone (both off-label)

products.name: Ketoconazole shampoo; supplements
products.actives: Ketoconazole; Midi-curated supplements

consultation: Video visit with a Midi clinician, covered by many insurers; hair is handled inside a whole menopause care plan (HRT, skin, nutrition, dermatologist referral).
distinctive: Insurance pays for the visit, which is rare in hair loss. Topical finasteride prescribed to midlife women. Also sells a prescription cream for unwanted facial hair, the opposite problem in the same patient.
sizeSignal: Available in all 50 states with insurance coverage (company claim); no hair numbers published.

name: Felix
description: One of Canada's largest general telehealth brands (weight loss, ED, hair, skin, mental health) with separate men's and women's hair-loss services.

products.name: Finasteride
products.actives: Finasteride 1 mg or 5 mg tablets, packs of 30 or 100
products.price: Hair-loss medication "starting at CA$41.23 per 30 pills" before the pharmacy fill fee; varies by province and refill schedule

products.name: Minoxidil
products.actives: Topical minoxidil (non-prescription in Canada; requested through a short assessment)

products.name: Women's hair-loss plan
products.actives: "Personalized treatment plan complete with products made to manage female hair loss" (prescription and non-prescription; actives not named publicly)

products.name: Initial visit
products.actives: Online assessment reviewed by a Canadian practitioner
products.price: CA$40 (shown as free on promotion, Nov 2026)

consultation: Online health assessment, then a treatment plan from a licensed Canadian practitioner (doctor or nurse practitioner), delivery and ongoing messaging. Direct insurance billing is offered.
distinctive: Scale and trust in Canada, plus direct billing to private insurers. A dedicated women's hair-loss route. Canadian rules limit what can be said publicly about prescription drugs, so product detail sits behind the assessment.
sizeSignal: "Trusted by over 1.8 million Canadians" (all conditions); 4.8 on Trustpilot (company claim).

name: Jack Health
description: Canadian men's health clinic selling personalised hair programmes, including a compounded three-active topical.

products.name: Hello Hair
products.actives: Topical spray or serum: minoxidil 5% + finasteride 0.1% + latanoprost 0.03% (strengths from Jack's own comparison article)

products.name: Halt + Regrow
products.actives: Finasteride tablet daily + minoxidil 5% serum

products.name: Minoxidil 5%
products.actives: Minoxidil 5% topical

products.name: Full & Thick Pack
products.actives: Supplement: zinc, biotin, saw palmetto, vitamin D3

products.name: Rosemary Oil
products.actives: Rosemary oil (cosmetic)

consultation: Hair quiz, then a free digital consultation (CA$0 visit fee) with a licensed provider; a partner pharmacy prepares and ships; messaging for questions and plan changes.
distinctive: Latanoprost (a prostaglandin eye-drop drug that lengthens the growth phase) added to topical finasteride and minoxidil: a triple topical not seen at the big US or UK brands. Also sells a C$99 quarterly 55-biomarker blood test under the same brand.
sizeSignal: "Trusted by 300,000 Canadians" in "more than 500 communities" (company claim, all conditions).

name: myRocky (Rocky Health)
description: Canadian online clinic (weight loss, sexual health, hair, mental health) with a combined finasteride and minoxidil foam as its lead hair product.

products.name: 2-in-1 Foam (Finasteride & Minoxidil Topical Foam)
products.actives: Finasteride + minoxidil in one topical foam (strengths not shown)
products.price: CA$185 for a 2-month supply (billed every 2 months)

products.name: Tablet and topical solution bundle
products.actives: Finasteride tablets + minoxidil solution

products.name: Minoxidil topical solution
products.actives: Minoxidil solution (dropper)

products.name: Finasteride tablets
products.actives: Finasteride tablets

consultation: Add a product to the cart to start an online consultation; licensed doctors, nurse practitioners and pharmacists review. Pause or cancel any time.
distinctive: A foam (not a spray or solution) that carries both finasteride and minoxidil. The combination is not a licensed product, so it must be made by a compounding pharmacy (inferred). Prices shown openly, which is unusual in Canada.
sizeSignal: "Trusted by 350K+ Canadians" (company claim, all conditions).

name: UPGUYS
description: Canadian men's online pharmacy and clinic for ED, hair loss and premature ejaculation.
audience: Men 18+ in every province and territory except Yukon.

products.name: Finasteride (generic Propecia)
products.actives: Finasteride 1 mg, 28 tablets

products.name: Minoxidil AM/PM
products.actives: Two "extra strength" minoxidil solutions, one for morning and one for night, 2 x 30 ml (strength not shown)

products.name: Finasteride + Minoxidil
products.actives: 28 finasteride 1 mg tablets + AM and PM minoxidil solutions

consultation: Online visit with a Canadian practitioner; prescription required before dispensing.
distinctive: Separate morning and evening minoxidil formulas (an AM/PM routine idea).
sizeSignal: "Trusted by more than 200,000 patients"; 4.9 from 2,600+ Google reviews (company claim).

name: Phoenix
description: Canadian men's digital health clinic; hair-loss care is an online assessment that can lead to finasteride.

products.name: Finasteride
products.actives: Finasteride (details behind the assessment)

consultation: Secure online assessment about hair loss, history and medicines; a licensed Canadian provider reviews and may ask for photos.
distinctive: Nothing distinctive found in hair.
sizeSignal: No numbers found.

name: Mosh and Moshy
description: Australian men's telehealth brand (since 2016) with tiered hair-loss plans, and a newer sister programme, Moshy, for women's hair loss.

products.name: Prevention Only
products.actives: Not disclosed publicly (Australian law bans advertising prescription medicines)

products.name: Prevention & Regrowth (most popular)
products.actives: Not disclosed; Mosh says its treatments "combine two active ingredients, in tablet or spray form"

products.name: Hair Loss Clinic Plan
products.actives: Not disclosed; "targets loss from multiple angles", optional vitamins and shampoo

products.name: Moshy women's hair programme
products.actives: Not disclosed; personalised plan
products.price: From A$69 (includes consult, support and delivery)

consultation: 5-minute quiz, photos and history, then an online consultation with an Australian practitioner; unlimited messaging with the hair team. Quarterly subscriptions.
distinctive: The widest set of guarantees seen in this sweep: 180-day money-back guarantee, a "reformulation guarantee" (treatment adjusted if too strong or causing side effects) and a price-match guarantee. "85+ possible plan variations". A separate women's brand.
sizeSignal: "Over 60,000 men" treated for hair; "over 150,000 Aussies" overall (company claims).

name: hub.health
description: Australian telehealth platform with three low-priced men's hair plans, including a personalised all-in-one capsule.

products.name: Regrowth: Receding Hair
products.actives: "Customised formulation" (actives not disclosed publicly)

products.name: Prevention & Regrowth: Thinning & Receding (most popular)
products.actives: Combined treatments "in one convenient capsule personalised to you"

products.name: Prevention: Thinning Hair
products.actives: Not disclosed

products.name: Consultation
products.actives: Flat-fee clinician consult (no Medicare rebate)

consultation: Online eligibility questionnaire, then a paid A$35 consult with a clinician ("all you need is a phone"). No lock-in subscriptions.
distinctive: The cheapest personalised capsule found (from about A$0.65 a day) and a 180-day satisfaction guarantee. Plans are named by hair pattern (receding, thinning, both), which makes choosing simple.
sizeSignal: "Trusted by 300,000+ Aussies" (company claim, all conditions).

name: The Hairy Pill
description: A single personalised, compounded once-daily pill for hair loss, developed by dermatologist Professor Rodney Sinclair (who also holds a patent related to sublingual minoxidil), with phone consultations by partner doctors.

products.name: The Hairy Pill subscription
products.actives: Personalised compounded capsule; ingredients are not listed online (the company cites advertising rules). Third-party reports say low-dose oral minoxidil with finasteride or dutasteride (men) plus vitamins: unverified
products.price: A$75 a month; first 3 months paid upfront (or 4 payments of A$56.25, or from A$10 a week)

consultation: Online quiz, then a doctor phone call; a pharmacist calls before express delivery. Unlimited telehealth reviews; doctors adjust strength, dose or ingredients over time.
distinctive: One pill instead of several products. "Side Effect Protect": dose or ingredient changes at no extra charge if side effects appear. Regular phone reviews with photo progress. Built on a named professor's clinic protocol. Publishes outcome data from 1,000 sampled patients treated for 12+ months.
sizeSignal: Launched 2020. Company cites a sample of "1,000 randomly sampled active patients treated for 12+ months", so the active base is larger than that.

name: Gro Clinics
description: Doctor-led hair-transplant clinic chain that also sells "Prescription Haircare" plans by telehealth.
audience: Men and women in Australia and New Zealand.

products.name: Mono plan
products.actives: One active ingredient, chosen after consultation (not named publicly)
products.price: From A$36.25 a month (12-month billing; 3- and 6-month billing also offered)

products.name: Combo plan
products.actives: Two active ingredients

products.name: Telehealth consultation
products.actives: 15-minute call with a practitioner

consultation: A real 15-minute telehealth call ("a real consultation, not a quiz") with a registered practitioner; plan "built from 37 treatment options"; delivered at a chosen interval.
distinctive: Sells a live consultation as the difference from quiz-based rivals. Pricing by number of actives (mono or combo). A path from medicine to in-person therapies and transplant surgery in the same company.
sizeSignal: 14 transplant clinic locations listed in Australia plus Auckland; "trusted by over 15,000 men and women" (company claim).

name: Hers Australia (formerly Juniper) and Hims Australia (formerly Pilot)
description: Hims & Hers bought Eucalyptus (owner of Pilot, Juniper, Kin and Software) in 2026 for up to US$1.15 billion. Pilot became Hims in August 2026 and Juniper became Hers on 12 October 2026, adding a women's hair programme.

products.name: Hers Hair programme
products.actives: "New, innovative formulations of clinically proven treatment options for hair regrowth" (actives and prices not given in the release)

consultation: Online consultation with Australian practitioners; 24/7 care team access (per the launch release).
distinctive: Shows where the market is heading: the US leader now owns the Australian leader and Europe's ZAVA, and is rolling the same personalised hair formulas into each country. Pilot itself is covered in a separate deep dive.
sizeSignal: Eucalyptus reported an annual revenue run-rate above US$450 million at the time of the deal; Juniper community of more than 27,000 women.

name: MySpring (Spring, Wellster Healthtech)
description: A leading German men's telehealth brand (Wellster Healthtech, Munich), selling finasteride tablets, minoxidil and a combined pack after an online doctor assessment.

products.name: Finasterid tablets
products.actives: Finasteride 1 mg film-coated tablets (Finasterid NIO)

products.actives: 98 finasteride 1 mg tablets + 3 x 60 ml minoxidil 5% solution (50 mg/ml), a 3-month supply

consultation: Online medical questionnaire reviewed by a doctor; prescription filled by a partner mail-order pharmacy; delivery in 2 to 3 working days.
distinctive: A cautionary tale for compounding: German pharmacy press reports a court fight over whether its batch-made finasteride-minoxidil solution ("Defektur") and its advertising of prescription medicines were lawful, reaching the Federal Court of Justice in February 2026 (outcome not found).
sizeSignal: Wellster reported EUR 50 million revenue and first full-year profit for 2025 (driven mainly by its weight-loss brand); "more than 2 million" people had used its platforms by 2022.

name: ZAVA (owned by Hims & Hers)

name: Charles
description: French men's health telehealth platform (sexual health, sleep, hair) offering fixed-price hair-loss teleconsultations with doctors under a protocol written by a hospital dermatologist.

products.name: Hair-loss teleconsultation

consultation: Questionnaire first, then a real doctor consultation by video, phone or secure messages, usually within 24 hours, 7 days a week; unlimited follow-up by message or phone.
distinctive: The patient chooses the channel (video, phone or chat) for the same fixed price. A named hospital dermatologist (Dr Pierre Schneider, Hôpital Saint-Louis) fronts the protocol.
sizeSignal: "Over 100,000 people have consulted" through Charles; 20,124 on-site reviews averaging 4.6/5 (company claims).

name: Hårklinikken

products.price: US$102 a bottle; 10% off on a 3-month subscription, 20% off on 6 months

sizeSignal: In business since 1992 (company claim); 4,106 reviews on the Extract page. No revenue figures found.

name: DoktorABC
description: Large German-language online prescription platform: a questionnaire reviewed by doctors, with medicines dispensed by a Dutch mail-order pharmacy or German partner pharmacies. Hair loss is one of 40+ categories.

name: Ulo

products.name: 0.005% Topical Finasteride (6-in-1), men

products.name: 0.2% Topical Dutasteride (6-in-1), men
products.actives: Dutasteride 0.2% + minoxidil 7% + tretinoin 0.01% + melatonin 0.01% + caffeine 0.2% + cetirizine 1%

products.name: 7% Topical Minoxidil (5-in-1)
products.actives: Minoxidil 7% + tretinoin + melatonin + caffeine + cetirizine (no DHT blocker)
products.price: From US$35 a month (men); from US$32 (women)

products.name: Oral options, men

products.price: From US$29, US$18 and US$22 a month

products.name: Sublingual Minoxidil, women

products.name: Oral Spironolactone combination, women
products.actives: Spironolactone 50 mg + minoxidil 0.625 mg + folic acid 1 mg + vitamin D 1000 IU (also spironolactone 200 mg alone; oral minoxidil 1.25 mg alone)
products.price: From US$59 a month (200 mg alone from US$44; minoxidil 1.25 mg from US$18)

products.name: 0.2% Topical Finasteride, postmenopausal women
products.actives: Finasteride 0.2% topical

consultation: 2-minute hair quiz matches a protocol; after purchase a short medical intake is reviewed by a licensed provider. Subscriptions include on-demand access to hair specialists and doctors.
distinctive: The most adventurous menu found: sublingual minoxidil, topical cetirizine (an antihistamine studied for hair), melatonin and caffeine boosters, micro-dose (0.005%) versus full-strength (0.2%) topical finasteride, topical dutasteride, 7% minoxidil, and no propylene glycol in any formula. The customer builds the treatment: delivery form, DHT reducer, growth stimulant, add-ons. 12-month (365-day) money-back guarantee.
sizeSignal: Small and young: about 65-70 Trustpilot reviews (mixed). No customer numbers published. The most detailed review is by its own co-founder (conflict of interest).

name: Shapiro MD (LifeMD)
description: Hair-loss brand owned by listed telehealth group LifeMD (which also owns Rex MD): a dermatologist-formulated shampoo, conditioner and foam system, minoxidil, a laser device and a telehealth prescription route.

products.name: Shapiro MD system (non-prescription)
products.actives: Shampoo, conditioner and leave-in foam with the brand's botanical DHT-blocking complex; over-the-counter minoxidil
products.price: Third-party estimates only: bundles about US$40-80 a month (unverified)

products.name: Prescription options
products.actives: Third-party reports: oral finasteride 1 mg, topical finasteride 0.25% solution, minoxidil 5% (unverified against the live site)

consultation: Online hair quiz; "hair growth experts" build a plan; prescription items need an online provider review. Free rush shipping.
distinctive: Hybrid of a mass-market infomercial-style cosmetic system and a prescription upsell under one brand.
sizeSignal: "Chosen by over 350,000 customers" (company claim). Parent LifeMD reported 2025 revenue of US$194.1 million across all brands.

name: Minoxidil Max
description: Long-running grey-market web shop for very high-strength minoxidil mixes (up to 15%) with finasteride, azelaic acid and retinoids, popular on hair-loss forums. Its site could not be reached from this research environment, so details below come from third-party listings.

products.name: DualGen-15 (with or without propylene glycol; "Plus" versions)
products.actives: Minoxidil 15% + azelaic acid 5%; "Plus" adds finasteride 0.1%, retinol or tretinoin 0.025% and caffeine
products.price: About US$42-50 per 2 oz (59 ml) bottle (third-party listings)

consultation: None reported (direct purchase). Whether any prescription check exists is unverified.
distinctive: Shows the demand for strengths above anything licensed (15% minoxidil) and for propylene-glycol-free bases. Not a model to copy: no clinical oversight.
sizeSignal: No figures. Listed on forum product databases (Tressless) for many years.

name: Retail pharmacy telehealth: Walgreens Virtual Healthcare and Optum
description: The big pharmacy and insurer groups now sell simple online hair-loss visits that lead to generic finasteride.

products.name: Walgreens men's hair-loss visit

products.name: Optum online care, hair loss

products.price: From US$15 a month (Optum page via search; a Healthline review quotes from US$10)

name: Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drugs

products.name: Finasteride 1 mg

products.name: Minoxidil tablets

sizeSignal: Widely covered national brand; no hair numbers.

name: Daniel Alain (Minoxidil Response Test)
description: Wig and hair-care company that sells a mail-in test to predict whether topical minoxidil will work for a person, plus its own minoxidil, an enzyme "booster" and an anti-shedding product.
audience: Men and women thinking about, or disappointed by, minoxidil.

products.name: Minoxidil Response Test (MRT)
products.actives: Plucked hairs are posted to the company's CLIA-certified lab, which measures the follicle enzyme (SULT1A1, a sulfotransferase) that switches minoxidil on
products.price: US$139 (or 4 payments of US$35); results in 1 to 2 weeks

products.name: INTACT Anti Hair Shedding Treatment; enzyme booster supplement
products.actives: Cosmetic anti-shedding treatment; supplement said to raise the enzyme

consultation: None (home test kit).
distinctive: A response-prediction test: "find out before you spend six months on it". Company-linked studies report about 93-95% sensitivity for predicting response; independent dermatologists quoted by Healthline were cautious. The company says only about half of men and 30-40% of women respond to topical minoxidil.
sizeSignal: Niche. No sales figures found.

name: Fagron TrichoTest
country: Netherlands / Belgium (sold through clinics and pharmacies in Europe, including the UK)
description: A cheek-swab DNA test from the compounding group Fagron. The report suggests which hair-loss actives should suit the patient, and a compounding pharmacy then makes that formula.
audience: Men and women, through clinicians and pharmacies.

products.name: TrichoTest
products.actives: Genetic test (Fagron cites 48 variations in 13-16 genes across 7 treatment categories; sources differ on the counts), with a report recommending personalised compounded formulas
products.price: About GBP 349-399 at a UK pharmacy; EUR 249-390 at a Lithuanian seller

consultation: Ordered through a clinician or pharmacist, who receives the report and prescribes or compounds from it.
distinctive: Links a diagnostic directly to a personalised compounded prescription. Evidence for its predictive value comes mainly from Fagron and sellers; treat with caution. Already available in the UK through clinics, so it is not a gap, but no UK online brand has built it into a consultation.
sizeSignal: Fagron is a global compounding supplier; test launched 2021.

name: Traya
description: A leading Indian hair-loss-only brand. A free online "Hair Test" assigns a root cause and a monthly kit that mixes dermatology, Ayurvedic herbs and nutrition, with a personal hair coach and a diet plan.

products.name: Customised monthly kit (Kits 1-6 by stage and cause)
products.actives: Doctor-prescribed plan combining dermatology products, Ayurvedic supplements (for example Hair Ras herbs), nutrition supplements, shampoo and scalp oil (the exact drug actives were not visible on the public page)
products.price: Individual items are priced about INR 190-800 each on the site; kit price depends on the plan

consultation: Online Hair Test (questions on family history, stress, gut, sleep, scalp) reviewed by doctors; a named hair coach follows up by phone and app; diet plan included.
distinctive: Treats hair loss as several root causes at once (genetics, nutrition, stress, gut, dandruff) and sells adherence: coach calls, an app with over 10 million installs ("1Cr+"), diet plans and rewards. Publishes its own outcome study ("93% saw results", 300 participants over 5+ months). Also earns from hair transplants.
sizeSignal: Revenue about INR 338 crore in the year to March 2025 (about GBP 30 million), up 43%, with a loss of about INR 23 crore after heavy marketing spend.

name: Man Matters (Mosaic Wellness)

products.price: Third-party price trackers quote kits from about INR 999 (unverified)

consultation: App-based doctor consultation; kits chosen by hair-loss stage.
distinctive: Home blood test booked in the app and tied to the hair plan. Kits sold by Norwood-style stage, which is easy for customers to understand.
sizeSignal: No figure verified in this sweep.
